proof:
Source: steps 1, 2, 7, 8 and 9 (the bound on Λ', on and off K) of the supplied proof of ts_fv_compact_variation_bounds, that is, the variation of Simon Ch. 4, 2.1 together with the uniform bounds of step (3.1) of the proof of ts_first_variation_of_pieces (the Jacobian computation of Simon Ch. 2, 5.2–5.3, as used for Ch. 4, 2.2), with an arbitrary δ ∈ (0, ε) in place of ε/2. No errata apply.

Notation. E := Ambient n ℓ with its Euclidean norm; L(E, E) := E →L[ℝ] E with the operator norm (a complete normed ring whose multiplication is composition and whose unit 1 is the identity I); U := (−ε, ε) × E = Ioo (−ε) ε ×ˢ univ ⊆ ℝ × E; Φ : ℝ × E → E, Φ(t, y) := φ t y; ι₁ := (1, 0) ∈ ℝ × E; ι₂ := ContinuousLinearMap.inr ℝ ℝ E ∈ L(E, ℝ × E), ι₂ v = (0, v); X(y) := deriv (t ↦ φ t y) 0; Dφ_t(y) := fderiv ℝ (φ t) y. (H1)–(H6) are the fields pos, compact, smooth, diffeo, init, fixed of IsCompactVariation φ ε K. Only (H1), (H2), (H3) and (H6) are used.

1. Preliminaries. U is open (isOpen_Ioo.prod isOpen_univ); by (H3), Φ is C^∞ at every q ∈ U (ContDiffOn.contDiffAt), hence differentiable there; DΦ := fderiv ℝ Φ is C^∞ on U (ContDiffOn.fderiv_of_isOpen, as ∞ + 1 ≤ ∞). By (H1), 0 ∈ (−ε, ε); by (H2), K is closed and Kᶜ is open.

2. The map G. Define G : ℝ × E → L(E, E), G(q) := DΦ(q) ∘ ι₂. G is DΦ followed by the fixed continuous linear map R : L(ℝ × E, E) → L(E, E), R(A) := A ∘ ι₂ (R = (ContinuousLinearMap.compL ℝ E (ℝ × E) E).flip ι₂), so G is C^∞ on U (ContDiffOn.clm_comp with contDiffOn_const). Consequently G is differentiable at every q ∈ U, and fderiv ℝ G is continuous on U (ContDiffOn.continuousOn_fderiv_of_isOpen).

3. Time slices. Let t ∈ (−ε, ε) and y ∈ E. Then φ t = Φ ∘ j_t with j_t(y') := (t, y'), whose derivative at y is ι₂ (HasFDerivAt.prodMk of hasFDerivAt_const and hasFDerivAt_id), and Φ is differentiable at (t, y) ∈ U. By the chain rule, HasFDerivAt (φ t) (G(t, y)) y; hence fderiv ℝ (φ t) y = G(t, y).

4. Definition of Λ'. For t ∈ ℝ and x ∈ E put Λ'(t, x) := (fderiv ℝ G (t, x)) ι₁ ∈ L(E, E).

5. The derivative (∗). Let x ∈ E and t ∈ (−ε, ε). G is differentiable at (t, x) ∈ U (step 2) and s ↦ (s, x) has derivative ι₁ at t (HasDerivAt.prodMk of hasDerivAt_id' and hasDerivAt_const), so by the chain rule (HasFDerivAt.comp_hasDerivAt) s ↦ G(s, x) has derivative (fderiv ℝ G (t, x)) ι₁ = Λ'(t, x) at t. For every s in the neighbourhood (−ε, ε) of t (Ioo_mem_nhds), fderiv ℝ (φ s) x = G(s, x) by step 3. Hence (HasDerivAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq) s ↦ fderiv ℝ (φ s) x has derivative Λ'(t, x) at t.

6. Λ'(0, x) = fderiv ℝ X x (symmetry of second derivatives). Fix x ∈ E. Φ is C^∞, in particular C², at (0, x) ∈ U. Let D := fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ Φ) (0, x), so (D a) b ∈ E for a, b ∈ ℝ × E. DΦ is C¹ at (0, x) (ContDiffAt.fderiv_right), hence has derivative D at (0, x).
(i) For every y ∈ E, X(y) = DΦ(0, y) ι₁: t ↦ (t, y) has derivative ι₁ at 0 and Φ is differentiable at (0, y) ∈ U, so the chain rule gives HasDerivAt (t ↦ φ t y) (DΦ(0, y) ι₁) 0. Thus X = ev_{ι₁} ∘ DΦ ∘ k, where k(y) := (0, y) has derivative ι₂ and ev_{ι₁}(A) := A ι₁ is continuous linear (ContinuousLinearMap.apply). By the chain rule at x, fderiv ℝ X x = ev_{ι₁} ∘ D ∘ ι₂, i.e. (fderiv ℝ X x) v = (D (ι₂ v)) ι₁ for every v ∈ E.
(ii) G = R ∘ DΦ with R continuous linear (step 2), so by the chain rule fderiv ℝ G (0, x) = R ∘ D, i.e. (fderiv ℝ G (0, x)) a = (D a) ∘ ι₂ for a ∈ ℝ × E. Hence Λ'(0, x) v = (D ι₁)(ι₂ v) for every v ∈ E.
(iii) Φ is C^∞ at (0, x) and minSmoothness ℝ 2 = 2 ≤ ∞, so the second derivative D is symmetric: (D a) b = (D b) a for all a, b ∈ ℝ × E (ContDiffAt.isSymmSndFDerivAt). Taking a = ι₁ and b = ι₂ v gives Λ'(0, x) v = (D ι₁)(ι₂ v) = (D (ι₂ v)) ι₁ = (fderiv ℝ X x) v for every v ∈ E; hence Λ'(0, x) = fderiv ℝ X x (ContinuousLinearMap.ext).

7. Part (i). By steps 5 and 6, for every x ∈ E: Λ'(0, x) = fderiv ℝ X x, and HasDerivAt (s ↦ fderiv ℝ (φ s) x) (Λ'(t, x)) t for every t ∈ (−ε, ε).

8. Part (ii). Fix δ with 0 < δ < ε. Q := [−δ, δ] × K is compact (isCompact_Icc.prod, (H2)) and Q ⊆ U since δ < ε. The map q ↦ (fderiv ℝ G q) ι₁ is continuous on U (step 2, composed with evaluation at the fixed vector ι₁: ContinuousOn.clm_apply with continuousOn_const), hence on Q, so there is B₂ ∈ ℝ with ‖(fderiv ℝ G q) ι₁‖ ≤ B₂ for all q ∈ Q (IsCompact.exists_bound_of_continuousOn). Put B := max(B₂, 0). Let x ∈ E and t ∈ (−δ, δ); then t ∈ (−ε, ε).
(a) Case x ∈ K. Then (t, x) ∈ Q, so ‖Λ'(t, x)‖ ≤ B₂ ≤ B.
(b) Case x ∉ K. W := (−ε, ε) × Kᶜ is an open set (isOpen_Ioo.prod) containing (t, x). For (s, y) ∈ W, φ s = id on the open neighbourhood Kᶜ of y by (H6), so φ s =ᶠ[𝓝 y] id and G(s, y) = fderiv ℝ (φ s) y = fderiv ℝ id y = I (step 3; Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq, fderiv_id). Thus G =ᶠ[𝓝 (t, x)] (fun _ ↦ I), so fderiv ℝ G (t, x) = fderiv ℝ (fun _ ↦ I) (t, x) = 0 and Λ'(t, x) = 0 ι₁ = 0. Hence ‖Λ'(t, x)‖ = 0 ≤ B.

9. Conclusion. The map Λ' of step 4 satisfies (i) by step 7 and (ii) by step 8. ∎
